acceptance: NOT A RECOVERY ACCEPTANCE: this only reports what COMMITTED, checksum-proven block-bitmap images say about the old extents after the deletion. No reuse observed is NOT proof that the bytes are intact; reuse observed is NOT proof of overwritten bytes. The candidate extent map alone is never accepted.
blockers: the image after the last live one is not the old inode unlinked
derived last-live/deletion-start tids 17169/None differ from the prior finding 17169/17170

window.tail: s_sequence - 1 never committed: clean unmount (jbd2_journal_destroy: j_tail_sequence = ++j_transaction_sequence), no header of that tid anywhere, s_head = the block after the newest commit

limits: commit granularity: an allocate+free of a block INSIDE one transaction leaves no bitmap trace (data may still have been written)

writes that never touch the bitmap are invisible: discard/TRIM (online 'discard' mount option or fstrim after the deletion), raw device or image-layer (qcow2) writes; the image layer must be checked separately (e.g. allocation map / sampled reads)
history before the oldest retained transaction cannot be proven absent; this check needs and verifies only tids >= the last live inode image
state after the newest journaled transaction is the current on-disk bitmap (checked separately: current-allocation.json)
block bitmap locations come from the current group descriptors (fs-stats); they are static unless the fs was resized
per-extent leaf tids are assigned from picked[].entries in logical order of the candidate map (used only for the pre-deletion check)
